standard_prerequisites.name: The f-divisibility condition on the inverse system
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma lemma-equivalent-f-good (tag 0H39), condition (1)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the identification F_n = F_{n+1}/f^n F_{n+1} that turns the connecting maps into multiplication by f^c.

core_obligations: Write down the exact sequence H^{p-1}(X, F_c) -> H^p(X, F_{n-c}) -> H^p(X, F_n) -> H^p(X, F_c) for the inverse system (proof lines 9281-9286).
Use that the first term H^{p-1}(X, F_c) is independent of n to choose a compatible sequence of liftings of the components (proof lines 9287-9289).
Package the liftings into an element of the limit and conclude that the original element equals f^c times it, giving both the kernel description and the f-adic identification (proof lines 9290-9291).
proof_roadmap: Produce the connecting sequence relating three consecutive levels.
Lift compatibly using independence of the first term from n.
Conclude the kernel description and the f-adic topology statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies, for an inverse system satisfying the divisibility condition of the equivalent-f-good lemma, the subgroup f^c H^p as the kernel of the natural map from the limit to the c-th term, and concludes that the limit topology is the f-adic topology. The proof takes an element in the kernel, uses the connecting exact sequence H^{p-1}(X, F_c) -> H^p(X, F_{n-c}) -> H^p(X, F_n) -> H^p(X, F_c) to lift the components compatibly, and observes that the first term is independent of n, which yields a compatible family giving the element as f^c times a limit (proof lines 9270-9291). H2: the compatible lifting through the connecting sequence is the whole content and is written out.
